selected_sources.title: Point4Cast: Streaming Dynamic Scene Reconstruction and Forecasting
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Highest exact-match relevance: official CVPR 2026 highlight explicitly targets streaming 2D video input, online updates, dynamic 3D reconstruction, forecasting, point maps, camera parameters, and scene flow.
selected_sources.expected_use: Primary source for the scoped question's core formulation: streaming video-to-3D point-map reconstruction and forecasting.

selected_sources.title: STream3R: Scalable Sequential 3D Reconstruction with Causal Transformer
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official ICLR 2026 accepted record with direct relevance to pointmap prediction, sequential/streaming image processing, causal attention, online 3D perception, and real-time streaming environments.
selected_sources.expected_use: Primary source for causal-transformer streaming pointmap reconstruction and scalability claims.

selected_sources.title: LASER: Layer-wise Scale Alignment for Training-Free Streaming 4D Reconstruction
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 record explicitly addresses streaming videos, point map reconstruction, memory limits, FPS, and training-free conversion of offline reconstruction models into streaming systems.
selected_sources.expected_use: Primary source for practical streaming conversion, scale alignment, runtime, and memory tradeoffs.

selected_sources.title: StreamSplat: Towards Online Dynamic 3D Reconstruction from Uncalibrated Video Streams
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official ICLR 2026 accepted record focused on online dynamic 3D reconstruction from uncalibrated arbitrary-length video streams under latency and memory constraints.
selected_sources.expected_use: Primary source for online feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting from video streams and comparison against optimization-heavy reconstruction.

selected_sources.title: V-DPM: Video Reconstruction with Dynamic Point Maps
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 record directly targets video reconstruction using dynamic point maps, extending point-map representations from image pairs to videos and dynamic 3D/4D content.
selected_sources.expected_use: Primary source for the dynamic point map representation and its role in video reconstruction.

selected_sources.title: DynamicVGGT: Learning Dynamic Point Maps for 4D Scene Reconstruction in Autonomous Driving
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 record on dynamic point maps and temporal correspondence for feed-forward 4D reconstruction, with future point-map prediction in autonomous driving scenes.
selected_sources.expected_use: Source for dynamic point-map learning, temporal coherence mechanisms, and driving-scene benchmarks.

selected_sources.title: Ov3R: Open-Vocabulary Semantic 3D Reconstruction from RGB Videos
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 highlight relevant to RGB video streams and dense point-map prediction, adding semantic reconstruction coverage beyond geometry-only methods.
selected_sources.expected_use: Source for semantic extensions of video-stream point-map reconstruction and Spatial AI framing.

selected_sources.title: MoRe: Motion-aware Feed-forward 4D Reconstruction Transrformer
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 highlight on efficient feed-forward dynamic 3D reconstruction from monocular videos with causal temporal attention, relevant even though the abstract does not foreground point maps.
selected_sources.expected_use: Source for feed-forward 4D reconstruction architecture, temporal attention, and dynamic/static disentanglement.

selected_sources.title: MotionCrafter: Repurposing Video Generators for Dense Geometry and Motion Reconstruction
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 highlight on monocular video 4D geometry and motion reconstruction using point maps and scene flows; relevant to video point-map reconstruction but less specifically online/streaming.
selected_sources.expected_use: Source for point-map and scene-flow latent representations in monocular video reconstruction.

selected_sources.title: MoVieS: Motion-Aware 4D Dynamic View Synthesis in One Second
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 record on fast monocular-video 4D scene reconstruction, geometry, motion, and 3D point tracking; relevant for efficient reconstruction although framed as view synthesis.
selected_sources.expected_use: Source for fast dynamic reconstruction and unified geometry/motion/view-synthesis claims.

selected_sources.title: ClipGStream: Clip-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Any Length and Any Motion Multi-View Dynamic Scene Reconstruction
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 record on clip-stream reconstruction for long dynamic multi-view videos; relevant to streamable reconstruction but based on Gaussian Splatting rather than point maps.
selected_sources.expected_use: Source for scalable long-sequence and clip-stream reconstruction design.

selected_sources.title: MoRGS: Efficient Per-Gaussian Motion Reasoning for Streamable Dynamic 3D Scenes
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official CVPR 2026 record on online dynamic-scene reconstruction from streaming multi-view inputs under low-latency constraints; selected for streaming reconstruction diversity despite not being point-map-centric.
selected_sources.expected_use: Source for online Gaussian-based dynamic reconstruction and motion reasoning contrasts.

selected_sources.title: $\pi^3$: Permutation-Equivariant Visual Geometry Learning
selected_sources.selection_rationale: Official ICLR 2026 accepted point-map reconstruction foundation model relevant as a backbone or comparator for streaming methods, though not itself primarily an online streaming-video paper.
selected_sources.expected_use: Background source for point-map prediction, visual-geometry backbone assumptions, and baseline context.

not_selected.title: KV-Tracker: Real-Time Pose Tracking with Transformers
not_selected.rejection_rationale: Official and partially relevant to real-time online tracking/reconstruction, but its center of gravity is 6-DoF pose tracking and KV caching rather than streaming video point-map reconstruction.

not_selected.title: Dens3R: A Foundation Model for 3D Geometry Prediction
not_selected.rejection_rationale: Official ICLR 2026 pointmap-related foundation-model record, but the abstract emphasizes unified dense geometry prediction rather than online, streaming, or video reconstruction.

not_selected.title: Geometry-aware 4D Video Generation for Robot Manipulation
not_selected.rejection_rationale: Official ICLR 2026 and uses pointmap alignment, but the task is geometry-aware future video generation for manipulation rather than reconstruction of online/streaming video into a 3D point map.

not_selected.title: Lyra: Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction via Video Diffusion Model Self-Distillation
not_selected.rejection_rationale: Official ICLR 2026 and related to dynamic 3D scene generation/reconstruction, but it is generative 3DGS self-distillation rather than online streaming video point-map reconstruction.

coverage_gaps: ICML 2026: the official OpenReview group exists, but its group metadata marks public_submissions=false. API queries for accepted venue labels ICML 2026 spotlight and ICML 2026 regular returned no public notes, and browser rendering found no source-like records. PMLR proceedings appear not yet available for ICML 2026 as of 2026-05-05. Search did not broaden beyond official ICML 2026 sources.

CVPR 2026: the CVPR virtual-site JSON currently exposes official virtual paper records and abstracts, but many records have paper_pdf_url=null. Direct official PDFs/CVF OpenAccess proceedings were not visible from the allowed official pages at search time.
The selected set is dominated by CVPR 2026 and ICLR 2026 because no official public ICML 2026 accepted-paper/proceedings records were available in the search artifact under the declared source scope.

Several selected sources address online or streamable reconstruction with Gaussian Splatting rather than explicit point maps; they are included for method diversity and should be treated as adjacent evidence during later reading and synthesis.
